exposure: Severity of COVID-19 (symptomless, mild, moderate, severe)
outcome: Clinical and laboratory characteristics (e.g., D-dimer levels)
cohort: The study included 295 pregnant women hospitalized with COVID-19, with a subset of 193 women who delivered under the circumstances of COVID-19.
finding: A considerable proportion of pregnant women with COVID-19 experienced maternal and delivery complications, particularly preterm birth and low birth weight, with moderate-severe COVID-19 showing significant inverse correlations with delivery week, birth weight, and APGAR scores.
mod_finding: Among the deliveries, 61.2% of cesarean sections were performed on an emergency basis.
cross-section timing: Data collected retrospectively from March 2020 to January 2023.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome, with low birth weight identified as a complication and inversely correlated with moderate-severe COVID-19.
gest_age: Measured as an outcome (delivery week, preterm birth), with delivery week inversely correlated with moderate-severe COVID-19.
